Maintenance Procedure Information System
 | Protection | Maintenance Procedures
Document No.: OCR-082-r0a | Equipment:
 Directional and Non-Directional Overcurrent and Earth Leakage Protection
 REX 521 HO4
 ABB
Issued to: 
 Distribution Companies
Status: 
 Draft
Approval date: 
 2009 | Procedure:
 Using a three-phase secondary injection device (voltage and current)
Next review date: 
 2014
Introduction
This document sets out the steps to be followed when testing and calibrating the Parallel Feeder Protection relay, as this device performs many functions, including directional and non-directional overcurrent and earth leakage protection, with event recording and current, voltage and power measurements, etc.
This document was prepared by North Cairo Electricity Distribution Company and was reviewed and approved by the MPIS coordinators.
Safety Precautions
Notify the competent control of the cells to be worked on by an approved official signal. | 
Issue an approved work order with all items completed. | 
Maintenance and test personnel must carry the occupational safety and health category card. | 
The cell circuit breaker shall be switched off by the competent operation technician on instructions from the competent control, and the circuit breaker placed in the test position. | 
Ensure warning signs are posted on the cells to be worked on. | 
Occupational safety and health instructions must be followed at the work site. | 
Ensure the correct phase sequence of voltage and current on the protection device. | 
Do not open any current transformer secondary circuits. | 
Do not short-circuit any secondary or primary voltage circuits.
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Three-phase secondary injection device (voltage and current), complete with connections, with load angle adjustment, e.g. ISADRT 6. | 
Phase sequence measuring device for the three phases of voltage and current (Power analyzer). | 
Tool bag including avometer, ammeter, screwdrivers of different sizes, cutters, strippers, etc. | 
Suitable laptop computer with the protection device operating software CAP 501 and the injection device. | 
Necessary connections for linking the laptop computer to the protection device and the injection device. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
Ensure the DC auxiliary voltage is present and measure -ve & +ve at the protection device at points (1,2) on terminal block X4.1 and compare it with the range available on the device. | 
Prepare the secondary injection device by connecting its leads and supplying it with the AC auxiliary voltage after measuring it and comparing it with the range available for it. | 2.
Review the setting values of the directional and non-directional overcurrent and earth leakage protections on the protection device and ensure they are correct. | 3.
First: Testing the Non-Directional Overcurrent Protection
Connect the injection device current leads to the protection device at points (1,2) on terminal block X1.1 | 1.
Raise the injection current gradually until reaching the pickup current Ipu of the protection device and record this value | 2.
Lower the injection current value gradually until the protection device releases, reaching the reset current Ireset of the protection device, and record this value | 3.
Calculate the reset factor (Reset factor = Ireset / Ipu); it must be greater than 95% for digital devices | 4.
Repeat these steps (6-5-4-3) for the second phase at points (4,5) on terminal block X1.1 and the third phase at points (7,8) on terminal block X1.1 | 5.
Connect the TRIP tripping leads of the protection device at points (1,4) on terminal block X4.2 to the Stop timer terminals of the injection device, raise the current to a value slightly above the pickup current, and calculate the tripping time and compare it with the protection device setting values | 6.
Second: Testing the Non-Directional Earth Leakage Protection
Connect the injection device current leads to the protection device at points (10,11) on terminal block X1.1 | 1.
Raise the injection current gradually until reaching the pickup current Ipu of the protection device and record this value | 2.
Lower the injection current value gradually until the protection device releases, reaching the reset current Ireset of the protection device, and record this value | 3.
Calculate the reset factor Reset factor = Ireset / Ipu; it must be greater than 95% for digital devices | 4.
Connect the Trip tripping leads of the protection device at points (1,4) on terminal block X4.2 to the Stop timer terminals of the injection device, raise the current to a value slightly above the pickup current, and calculate the tripping time and compare it with the protection device setting values | 5.
Third: Testing the Directional Overcurrent Protection
Ensure the secondary voltage terminals of the voltage transformers are isolated on the protection device by switching off the automatic switch of the voltage transformers in the cell | 1.
Connect the injection device leads to the voltage and current windings of the protection device, observing polarity and phase order, noting that: the current windings of the protection device are at points (1,2)/(4,5)/(7,8) on terminal block X1.1, star connection; the voltage windings of the protection device are at points (19,21)/(22,24)/(25,27) on terminal block X1.1, delta connection | 2.
Raise the injection voltage gradually until reaching the Start voltage of the protection device | 3.
Raise the injection current gradually until reaching the Start current of the protection device | 4.
Change the load angle between voltage and current on the injection device from zero to 359 to find the device trips in the range from (Q-85) to (Q+85), where the operation direction setting Oper-direction is forward on the protection device, and in the range from (Q-95) to (Q+265), where the operation direction setting Oper-direction is reverse on the protection device, where Q is the Basic angle value set on the protection device, which can be set in the range (zero : +90) | 5.
Connect the Trip tripping leads of the protection device at points (1,4) on terminal block X4.2 to the Stop timer terminals of the injection device to measure the tripping time and compare it with the protection device setting values | 6.
Calculate the reset factor by the aforementioned method; it must be greater than 95% for digital devices | 7.
Fourth: Testing the Directional Earth Leakage Protection
Ensure the secondary voltage terminals of the voltage transformers are isolated on the protection device by switching off the automatic switch of the voltage transformers in the cell | 1.
Connect the injection device leads to the voltage and current windings of the protection device, observing polarity, noting that: the current winding of the protection device is at points (10,11) on terminal block X1.1; the voltage winding of the protection device is at points (16,18) on terminal block X1.1 | 2.
Raise the injection voltage gradually until reaching the Start voltage of the protection device | 3.
Raise the injection current gradually until reaching the Start current of the protection device | 4.
Change the load angle between voltage and current on the injection device from zero to 359 to find the device trips in the range from (Q-S) to (Q+S), where the operation direction setting Oper-direction is forward on the protection device, and from (Q-180-S) to (Q+180+S), where the operation direction setting Oper-direction is reverse on the protection device, where Q is the Basic angle value set on the protection device, which can be set in the range (zero : -90), and S is the operation sector range Oper-sector, which can be set to (80 or 88) | 5.
Connect the Trip tripping leads of the protection device at points (1,4) on terminal block X4.2 to the Stop timer terminals of the injection device to measure the tripping time and compare it with the protection device setting values | 6.
Calculate the reset factor by the aforementioned method; it must be greater than 95% for digital devices | 7.
Fifth: Setting and Testing the Directional Protection Device on Normal Load
Ensure the cell load is greater than the lowest setting value of the protection device, namely: directional overcurrent > 0.05 In; directional earth leakage > 0.05 In | 1.
Ensure the correct phase sequence of voltage and current at the protection device terminals Vr-Ir, Vs-Is, Vt-It, using the Power analyzer | 2.
Setting and Testing the Directional Overcurrent
Determine the load angle and direction from the Power analyzer: whether it is in the first quadrant or the third quadrant | 1.
Set the Basic angle value on the protection device to a value in the range (zero to +90), e.g. (60) | 2.
Set the protection device to directional mode in the same direction as the load angle, by setting the operation direction type Oper-direction on the protection device to Forward if the load angle is in the first quadrant, and Reverse if the load angle is in the third quadrant | 3.
Lower the current setting value of the directional overcurrent protection to a value below the normal load value; in this case the device operates with directional overcurrent protection for the three phases | 4.
Reverse the operation direction type Oper-direction on the protection device to become opposite to the load angle direction; in this case the device does not operate with directional overcurrent protection for any phase, although the current setting value for directional overcurrent is below the normal load value | 5.
Fix the operation direction type Oper-direction on the protection device to become opposite to the load angle direction and set the directional overcurrent protection current value to the values in use | 6.
Directional Earth Leakage
Disconnect the R-phase fuse of the voltage transformer from the primary side, following occupational safety and health instructions at the work site, so that the open delta voltage appears on the voltage winding of the protection device to operate the directional earth leakage protection | 1.
Lower the setting current value of the directional earth leakage protection to a value below the normal load value | 2.
Set the Basic angle values on the protection device to a value in the range (-90 to zero), e.g. (-30) | 3.
Test the directionality by two methods, namely:- | 4.
First Method
Make a bridge across phases (S,T) with the neutral point N of the secondary terminals of the current transformers on the protection device; current then passes through phase R in the earth leakage winding of the protection device. If directional earth leakage pickup occurs, reverse the operation direction type Oper-direction and repeat the test on phases (S,T) until pickup does not occur. | 
Repeat the test by bridging phases (T,R) so that current passes for phase S in the earth leakage winding and pickup occurs. | 
Repeat the test by bridging phases (R,T) so that current passes for phase T in the earth leakage winding and pickup occurs; this is then the directionality angle of the directional earth leakage protection on which the device is set. | 
Second Method
Make a bridge across phase (R) with the neutral point N of the secondary terminals of the current transformers on the protection device; current then passes through phases (S,T) in the earth leakage winding of the protection device opposite to the direction of phase R. If directional earth leakage pickup does not occur, reverse the operation direction type Oper-direction until pickup occurs. | 
Repeat the test by bridging phase (S) so that the current of phases (T,R) passes opposite to the direction of phase (S) in the earth leakage winding and pickup does not occur. | 
Repeat the test by bridging phase (T) so that the current of phases (R,S) passes opposite to the direction of phase (T) in the earth leakage winding and pickup does not occur; this is then the directionality angle of the directional earth leakage protection on which the device is set. | 
Reconnect the R-phase fuse of the voltage transformer from the primary side, following occupational safety and health instructions, and disconnect the S-phase fuse and follow the previous steps, and likewise with phase T, to confirm the test | 5.
